selected_modules.reason: The issue is a C++20 coroutines regression involving temporary awaitables and destructor timing. The C++ front end owns coroutines support and C++ object lifetime/destructor semantics before middle-end lowering, making it the most likely upstream source.

The pass trace explicitly shows the coroutine-specific pass tree-coro-lower-builtins. That points to middle-end coroutine lowering on GIMPLE as an active execution stage. A bug where temporary awaitables are destroyed too early can arise during coroutine lowering/rewriting of suspend points and temporaries into GIMPLE form.
